question: Nose wheel shimmy is controlled by:
correct_answer: A shimmy damper
explanation: A shimmy damper absorbs and dissipates rapid side-to-side steering oscillations of the nose wheel. It prevents the oscillation from building during taxi, take-off, or landing.

question: The blade angle of a propeller is the angle:
option_a: Between the chord line and the plane of rotation
option_b: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
option_d: Bending the blade in the opposite direction to the rotation
correct_answer: Between the chord line and the plane of rotation
explanation: Propeller blade angle is measured between the blade chord and the plane of rotation. It is a geometric setting, unlike angle of attack, which is measured relative to the local airflow.

question: In the tyre size "28 x 12.00-10", the figure "12.00" represents:
correct_answer: The tyre width
explanation: In the designation 28 x 12.00-10, 12.00 is the nominal tyre section width in inches. The first number is outside diameter and the final number is bead or rim diameter.

question: A fuselage which is constructed to allow the skin to take some of the load is:
correct_answer: A semi-monocoque structure
explanation: A semi-monocoque fuselage combines internal formers and stringers with stressed skin. The framework maintains the shape while the skin carries part of the flight and ground loads.

question: The torque created by a rotating propeller has the effect on the propeller of:
option_a: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
option_b: A coarse pitch propeller will produce a better cruise performance than a fine pitch propeller
option_c: Bending the blade in the opposite direction to the rotation
correct_answer: Bending the blade in the opposite direction to the rotation
explanation: The engine applies torque in the direction of rotation while aerodynamic resistance and blade inertia oppose it. The resulting load tends to bend or twist each blade opposite the direction of rotation.

question: The blade angle of a propeller varies from hub to tip in order to:
option_b: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
option_c: Bending the blade in the opposite direction to the rotation
option_d: A coarse pitch propeller will produce a better cruise performance than a fine pitch propeller
correct_answer: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
explanation: A blade section near the tip travels much faster than one near the hub. Reducing blade angle toward the tip keeps the local angle of attack and loading more nearly uniform along the blade.

question: Torsion is the term used to describe the load on an airframe:
correct_answer: Caused by twisting
explanation: Torsion is a twisting load produced when opposing forces or moments act about a structural member's axis. Airframes must resist it without permanent deformation.

question: Identify the flap type shown in Figure 2:
correct_answer: Split flap
explanation: A split flap deflects only the lower rear portion of the wing while the upper surface remains fixed. It creates substantial drag with a smaller lift increase than slotted or Fowler designs.

question: In order to remove the aerodynamic forces from the controls, balance tabs are adjusted by the pilot in flight:
option_a: Helps generate aerodynamic lift to prevent tail boom from dipping
option_b: A servo tab is connected directly to the pilot controls
option_c: Remains in the same position irrespective of the deflection of the control surface
option_d: To operate in the opposite direction to the primary control surface to which they are attached
correct_answer: To operate in the opposite direction to the primary control surface to which they are attached
explanation: A balance tab moves opposite to the primary control surface. Its aerodynamic force helps move that surface, reducing the control force the pilot must apply.

question: An adjustable trim tab when attached to an elevator will, when the elevator is moved:
option_a: To operate in the opposite direction to the primary control surface to which they are attached
option_b: Remains in the same position irrespective of the deflection of the control surface
option_c: Allow the aeroplane to fly at a higher angle of attack and lower airspeed
option_d: Helps generate aerodynamic lift to prevent tail boom from dipping
correct_answer: Remains in the same position irrespective of the deflection of the control surface
explanation: An adjustable trim tab keeps the angle selected by the pilot relative to the elevator until the trim setting is changed. Ordinary elevator movement does not re-command the tab.

question: A semi-cantilever monoplane is:
option_a: One where bracing struts mounted at the base of the fuselage are attached to the wings to provide additional support
option_c: The shape and rigidity of the fuselage is provided by formers and stringers whilst the stressed skin carries part of the load
option_d: All flight loads are carried by the outer skin
correct_answer: One where bracing struts mounted at the base of the fuselage are attached to the wings to provide additional support
explanation: A semi-cantilever wing carries part of its load internally and receives additional support from external bracing struts. A full cantilever wing needs no external bracing.

question: The main longitudinal member in a Truss type of fuselage construction would be:
correct_answer: Longeron
explanation: Longerons run lengthwise through a truss fuselage and carry major bending and longitudinal loads. Bracing members connect them to form the load-carrying framework.

question: The part of the wing to which the ailerons and flaps are usually attached is the:
correct_answer: Rear or auxiliary spar
explanation: The rear, or auxiliary, spar supports the wing's trailing-edge structure and commonly provides the hinge attachment for ailerons and flaps.

question: An under-inflated tyre may result in:
option_a: Excessive tread wear in the centre of the tyre
option_c: Excessive tread wear on the outer edges of the tyre
option_d: A blow-out may occur on landing because tyre movement may cause the inflation valve to be broken off from the tube
correct_answer: Excessive tread wear on the outer edges of the tyre
explanation: Low inflation lets the tyre sidewalls flex excessively and concentrates the load on the shoulders. The result is overheating and accelerated wear on the outer edges of the tread.

question: If the centre of gravity is moved aft during flight the effect will be:
correct_answer: To reduce longitudinal stability
explanation: Moving the centre of gravity aft reduces the distance between the CG and the aerodynamic centre. This weakens the restoring pitching moment and therefore reduces longitudinal stability.

question: Newton's second law refers to:
correct_answer: Acceleration and deceleration
explanation: Newton's second law states that a net force produces acceleration: F = ma. Acceleration includes speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.

question: The effect of slats is to:
option_a: Allow the aeroplane to fly at a higher angle of attack and higher airspeed
option_b: Allow the aeroplane to fly at a lower angle of attack and lower airspeed
option_c: Allow the aeroplane to fly at a higher angle of attack and lower airspeed
option_d: Helps generate aerodynamic lift to prevent tail boom from dipping
correct_answer: Allow the aeroplane to fly at a higher angle of attack and lower airspeed
explanation: A deployed slat opens a leading-edge slot that feeds energetic air over the upper wing surface. This delays airflow separation, allowing a higher angle of attack and a lower stall speed.

question: The reduction in the blade angle of a propeller towards the tip ensures that the thrust is constant along the blade and is referred to as:
correct_answer: Helical twist
explanation: Helical twist is the progressive reduction in blade angle from root to tip. It compensates for the higher rotational speed of the outer blade and helps distribute thrust efficiently.

question: The stall warning device, which is usually mounted on the leading edge of a wing, is adjusted to activate the cockpit warning:
correct_answer: Just before the stall
explanation: A stall warning is set to activate shortly before the wing reaches its critical angle of attack. The advance warning gives the pilot time to reduce angle of attack before the stall develops.

question: Tyre creep may cause:
option_a: The inflation valve to break away from the inner tube
option_b: A blow-out may occur on landing because tyre movement may cause the inflation valve to be broken off from the tube
option_c: Excessive tread wear on the outer edges of the tyre
option_d: Excessive tread wear in the centre of the tyre
correct_answer: The inflation valve to break away from the inner tube
explanation: Tyre creep is movement of the tyre relative to the wheel rim. If the inner tube moves with the tyre, the valve stem can be pulled sideways and torn away.

question: Tyre creep is most likely to occur as a result of:
correct_answer: Heavy braking on landing
explanation: Heavy braking applies a large tangential force between the tyre and rim. If friction at the bead is insufficient, the tyre slips around the rim and the creep marks move out of alignment.

question: As the angle of attack of an aerofoil in normal flight is increased, the centre of pressure will:
correct_answer: Move forward
explanation: Below the stall, increasing angle of attack changes the pressure distribution so the centre of pressure generally moves forward. This also changes the wing's pitching moment.

question: The most important structural component of a wing is:
correct_answer: The main spar
explanation: The main spar is the wing's principal load-carrying beam. It resists most of the bending and shear created by lift, aircraft weight, and landing loads.

question: Torque links may be incorporated on the nose shock struts of some undercarriage systems in order to:
option_a: The torque links are worn or have failed
option_b: Shock struts comprising a lower chamber containing hydraulic fluid and an upper chamber containing compressed air or nitrogen
option_c: The inflation valve to break away from the inner tube
option_d: Prevent the shock-strut piston and nose wheel from rotating within the cylinder
correct_answer: Prevent the shock-strut piston and nose wheel from rotating within the cylinder
explanation: Torque links join the moving and fixed parts of a nose oleo. They prevent relative rotation, keep the wheel aligned, and transmit steering inputs while still allowing vertical shock-strut movement.

question: The figure "10" indicated in the tyre size number "28 x 12.00-10" represents:
correct_answer: The bead diameter
explanation: The final figure in 28 x 12.00-10 is the bead-seat, or rim, diameter in inches. It identifies the wheel diameter on which the tyre is designed to fit.

question: Identify the flap type shown in Figure 4:
correct_answer: Slotted flap
explanation: A slotted flap leaves a passage between the wing and flap. High-energy air flowing through the slot delays separation over the flap, producing more lift at large deflections.

question: A shimmy in the nose wheel whilst taxying indicates that:
option_a: The torque links are worn or have failed
correct_answer: The torque links are worn or have failed
explanation: Worn or failed torque links allow unwanted rotational play between the nose wheel and shock strut. That looseness can develop into rapid alternating steering motion, or shimmy.

question: The most likely cause of under-extension of an oleo undercarriage leg is:
correct_answer: Low air pressure
explanation: Compressed air or nitrogen extends an oleo leg when the aircraft load is removed. If the gas pressure is too low, the strut sits lower than its normal extension.

question: Identify the flap type shown in Figure 1:
correct_answer: Fowler flap
explanation: A Fowler flap first travels rearward and then downward. Rearward movement increases wing area, while downward deflection increases camber, giving a large lift increase and useful drag for landing.

question: Newton's third law refers to:
correct_answer: Action and reaction
explanation: Newton's third law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. A propeller accelerates air rearward, for example, and the reaction provides forward thrust.

question: The operation of an oleo leg is based on:
option_a: Shock struts comprising a lower chamber containing hydraulic fluid and an upper chamber containing compressed air or nitrogen
option_b: A blow-out may occur on landing because tyre movement may cause the inflation valve to be broken off from the tube
option_c: Prevent the shock-strut piston and nose wheel from rotating within the cylinder
option_d: The inflation valve to break away from the inner tube
correct_answer: Shock struts comprising a lower chamber containing hydraulic fluid and an upper chamber containing compressed air or nitrogen
explanation: An oleo combines a compressible gas spring with hydraulic damping. The gas absorbs the landing load while oil forced through a restricted orifice controls the rate of compression and rebound.

question: An aircraft which has its CG too far aft would:
option_d: Be difficult to control in pitch
correct_answer: Be difficult to control in pitch
explanation: An excessively aft CG gives the tail less leverage to restore pitch disturbances. The aircraft becomes less stable, more sensitive in pitch, and harder to recover from a stall.

question: A rotating propeller will produce a force which acts in the opposite direction of rotation. This force is called:
correct_answer: Torque
explanation: Driving the propeller in one direction produces an equal reaction torque on the engine and airframe in the opposite direction, in accordance with Newton's third law.

question: Identify the flap type shown in Figure 3:
correct_answer: Plain flap
explanation: A plain flap is a simple hinged section of the trailing edge. Lowering it increases wing camber, which raises lift but also increases drag.

question: Ignoring crosswind, an aeroplane with a tricycle undercarriage and a clockwise-rotating propeller, as viewed from the cockpit, will tend to:
correct_answer: Yaw to the left
explanation: With a clockwise propeller viewed from the cockpit, reaction torque, asymmetric blade effect at high power, and spiralling slipstream all contribute to a left-yawing tendency during take-off.

question: The most likely cause of over-extension of an oleo undercarriage leg is:
correct_answer: High air pressure
explanation: Excessive air or nitrogen pressure produces too much extending force in an oleo. The strut therefore stands higher or extends farther than the specified normal position.

question: In a Truss or Girder-type fuselage, the main structural component is a:
correct_answer: Longeron
explanation: A longeron is a principal longitudinal member in a truss or girder fuselage. Together with cross-members and bracing, it carries the primary structural loads.

question: If the creep marks on the tyres have moved too far out of alignment:
option_a: The torque links are worn or have failed
option_b: A blow-out may occur on landing because tyre movement may cause the inflation valve to be broken off from the tube
option_c: Shock struts comprising a lower chamber containing hydraulic fluid and an upper chamber containing compressed air or nitrogen
option_d: Prevent the shock-strut piston and nose wheel from rotating within the cylinder
correct_answer: A blow-out may occur on landing because tyre movement may cause the inflation valve to be broken off from the tube
explanation: Creep marks show whether the tyre has moved on the rim. Excessive movement can drag and tear the inner-tube valve stem, causing sudden deflation or a blow-out.

question: A semi-monocoque fuselage design is one in which:
option_b: One where bracing struts mounted at the base of the fuselage are attached to the wings to provide additional support
option_c: All flight loads are carried by the outer skin
option_d: The shape and rigidity of the fuselage is provided by formers and stringers whilst the stressed skin carries part of the load
correct_answer: The shape and rigidity of the fuselage is provided by formers and stringers whilst the stressed skin carries part of the load
explanation: In semi-monocoque construction, formers and stringers establish the fuselage shape and reinforce it, while the stressed skin shares the applied loads. Damage to either can reduce structural strength.

question: A monocoque airframe structure is one where:
option_b: All flight loads are carried by the outer skin
option_c: One where bracing struts mounted at the base of the fuselage are attached to the wings to provide additional support
correct_answer: All flight loads are carried by the outer skin
explanation: In true monocoque construction the external shell carries essentially all flight loads. The absence of a heavy internal truss saves weight, but skin damage can seriously weaken the structure.

question: The primary load carrying component of an aluminium stressed skin wing is:
correct_answer: The main spar
explanation: The main spar is the primary beam in a stressed-skin wing. The skin helps carry torsion and shear, but the spar carries most of the wing-bending load.

question: The figure "28" indicated in the tyre size number "28 x 12.00-10" represents:
correct_answer: The outside diameter
explanation: In 28 x 12.00-10, the first figure is the tyre's approximate overall outside diameter in inches. The middle figure is width and the last is bead diameter.

question: An over-inflated tyre may result in:
option_a: Excessive tread wear on the outer edges of the tyre
option_b: Excessive tread wear in the centre of the tyre
option_d: A blow-out may occur on landing because tyre movement may cause the inflation valve to be broken off from the tube
correct_answer: Excessive tread wear in the centre of the tyre
explanation: Over-inflation crowns the tread and puts more load on its centre. This produces excessive centre wear and also reduces the tyre's ability to absorb shocks.

question: The components of a stressed skin wing which provide both strength and shape are called:
correct_answer: Ribs
explanation: Ribs give a wing its aerofoil shape and transfer skin and aerodynamic loads to the spars. They also support the skin against buckling.

question: With reference to tab balances:
option_a: A servo tab is connected directly to the pilot controls
option_b: Move in the same direction as the control surface
option_c: The centre of gravity is located forward of centre of pressure
option_d: Helps generate aerodynamic lift to prevent tail boom from dipping
correct_answer: A servo tab is connected directly to the pilot controls
explanation: With a servo tab, the pilot's control input moves the tab. Aerodynamic force on the tab then drives the main control surface, reducing the force required at the controls.

question: An anti-balance, or anti-servo, tab which is incorporated in a stabilator will:
option_a: A servo tab is connected directly to the pilot controls
option_b: To operate in the opposite direction to the primary control surface to which they are attached
option_c: Move in the same direction as the control surface
option_d: The centre of gravity is located forward of centre of pressure
correct_answer: Move in the same direction as the control surface
explanation: An anti-servo tab moves in the same direction as a stabilator. This increases the aerodynamic hinge moment and provides progressively heavier control feel, helping prevent over-control.

question: The horizontal stabiliser on the tail:
option_a: Provides longitudinal stability by generating an upward or downward force as required
option_b: Provides directional stability by generating sideways forces
option_c: Always generates an upward lift force to hold the tail up
option_d: Provides lateral stability by resisting roll
correct_answer: Provides longitudinal stability by generating an upward or downward force as required
explanation: The horizontal stabiliser (tailplane) provides longitudinal stability, returning the aircraft to balanced flight in pitch. It does this by generating an upward or a downward force as required, depending on the position of the centre of gravity and the flight condition; directional stability comes from the fin.

question: Newton's first law refers to:
correct_answer: Equilibrium
explanation: Newton's first law describes inertia: an object remains at rest or continues at constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force. With no net force, the object is in equilibrium.

question: The type of flap which, when extended, increases the surface area of the wing is called a:
correct_answer: Fowler flap
explanation: A Fowler flap moves rearward as it extends, increasing the wing's effective area before adding camber through downward deflection. This produces a particularly large lift increase.

question: During a normal level flight, the reduction in power will cause the nose of an aeroplane to drop because:
option_a: Allow the aeroplane to fly at a higher angle of attack and lower airspeed
option_b: The centre of gravity is located forward of centre of pressure
option_c: Helps generate aerodynamic lift to prevent tail boom from dipping
option_d: A servo tab is connected directly to the pilot controls
correct_answer: The centre of gravity is located forward of centre of pressure
explanation: With the CG ahead of the centre of pressure, the aircraft has a natural nose-down pitching tendency that is balanced in steady flight. Reducing power upsets that balance and the nose tends to lower.

question: The control of fuel entering the carburettor is achieved by:
option_a: The needle valve and the float chamber
correct_answer: The needle valve and the float chamber
explanation: A float maintains the fuel level in the carburettor chamber. As the level rises it pushes the needle valve toward its seat, reducing or stopping the incoming fuel flow.

question: The purpose of baffles in an aircraft's fuel tank is to:
option_a: A fuel vent in the fuel tank cap
option_b: Have an earth lead between ground, fuel truck, fuel nozzle and the aircraft
option_c: To allow atmospheric pressure to be retained in the tank as the fuel is used
option_d: Prevent the fuel from surging about during the flight
correct_answer: Prevent the fuel from surging about during the flight
explanation: Fuel-tank baffles restrict rapid fuel movement. Reducing surge keeps the pickup covered, limits sudden centre-of-gravity changes, and reduces structural loads inside the tank.

question: When the mixture control lever is moved to the full rich position:
option_a: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be decreased
option_b: The mixture should be in the full lean position until the engine fires and then richened slowly to keep the engine running
option_c: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be increased
option_d: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
correct_answer: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be increased
explanation: Moving the mixture control toward full rich increases the metered fuel flow for the available air. This lowers the air-to-fuel ratio and is normally required for high-power operation, subject to the POH.

question: During the operation of a reciprocating engine the piston is travelling up during:
correct_answer: The compression and exhaust strokes
explanation: The piston moves upward on compression to squeeze the fresh charge, and upward again on exhaust to expel burned gases. Induction and power are the two downward strokes.

question: Moving the mixture control to the lean position will:
option_a: The mixture should be in the full lean position until the engine fires and then richened slowly to keep the engine running
option_b: Reduce the amount of fuel entering the diffuser
option_c: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_d: Will also richen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
correct_answer: Reduce the amount of fuel entering the diffuser
explanation: Leaning moves the carburettor's mixture metering system toward a smaller fuel flow. Less fuel reaches the diffuser for approximately the same airflow, increasing the air-to-fuel ratio.

question: In a piston engine, the piston will have passed BDC and be moving towards TDC during:
correct_answer: The compression and exhaust strokes
explanation: After bottom dead centre, the piston travels upward during compression and exhaust. The valves determine whether it compresses a fresh charge or pushes burned gas out.

question: The term "valve lead" refers to:
option_a: The inlet valve closes after the piston has passed bottom dead centre
option_b: Lead fouling of the spark plugs
option_c: Should not be used because it may result in detonation, reduced power and lead fouling of the spark plugs
option_d: The inlet valve opening prior to the piston reaching TDC
correct_answer: The inlet valve opening prior to the piston reaching TDC
explanation: Valve lead means a valve begins opening before the piston reaches the nominal changeover point. Opening the inlet slightly before TDC helps establish flow for the next induction stroke.

question: During take-off in an aeroplane equipped with a Constant Speed Unit (CSU), it would be most beneficial to have:
correct_answer: A small blade angle
explanation: A small, or fine, blade angle lets the engine reach high RPM and develop take-off power at low forward speed. It is analogous to selecting a low gear for acceleration.

question: In the four-stroke piston engine, the term "valve lag" is used to indicate that the:
option_a: The inlet valve closes after the piston has passed bottom dead centre
option_b: The inlet valve closes before the piston has passed bottom dead centre
option_c: The inlet valve opening prior to the piston reaching TDC
option_d: The short period that both inlet and exhaust valves are both open around TDC
correct_answer: The inlet valve closes after the piston has passed bottom dead centre
explanation: Valve lag means a valve remains open beyond a dead-centre position. The inlet closes after BDC so the momentum of the incoming charge can continue filling the cylinder.

question: The purpose of a needle mixture control in a carburettor is to:
option_a: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_b: Will also richen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
option_c: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
option_d: Regulate the flow of fuel from the float chamber to the diffuser
correct_answer: Regulate the flow of fuel from the float chamber to the diffuser
explanation: The mixture needle varies the effective fuel passage between the float chamber and diffuser. Moving it changes fuel flow without directly changing the throttle airflow.

question: The application of carburettor heat:
option_a: Will also leanen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
option_b: Will also richen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
option_c: Will also richen the mixture because of the lower air temperature
option_d: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
correct_answer: Will also richen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
explanation: Carburettor heat supplies warmer, less-dense air. With less air mass but initially similar fuel flow, the mixture becomes richer and engine power or RPM normally falls.

question: When leaning the fuel/air mixture:
option_b: The ratio of fuel to air reduces
correct_answer: The ratio of fuel to air reduces
explanation: Leaning reduces fuel flow relative to airflow, so the fuel-to-air ratio decreases. Excessive leaning can cause rough running, high temperatures, and loss of power.

question: Moving the mixture control to the rich position will:
option_a: Increase the amount of fuel entering the diffuser
option_b: decrease the amount of fuel entering the diffuser
option_c: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_d: Will also richen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
correct_answer: Increase the amount of fuel entering the diffuser
explanation: Moving the mixture control toward rich opens the metering passage and increases fuel flow to the diffuser. The resulting mixture contains more fuel for the same mass of air.

question: After about 20 minutes flight with full tanks the engine stops but restarts immediately after selection of another tank, a possible cause was:
correct_answer: A blocked fuel tank vent
explanation: A blocked tank vent prevents air replacing the fuel being consumed. A partial vacuum gradually develops until fuel flow stops; selecting a properly vented tank restores the supply.

question: Prior to starting the engine of a carburettor equipped aircraft engine, the manual primer pump should be used, for easier starting, in order to supply additional fuel:
option_a: The engine starting to run rough and a decrease in RPM
option_b: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_c: Discharge additional fuel into the venturi
option_d: Into the induction system close to the inlet valves
correct_answer: Into the induction system close to the inlet valves
explanation: A primer bypasses the normal carburettor metering path and delivers fuel close to the inlet valves. This creates a combustible charge during cranking, especially when a cold engine vaporizes fuel poorly.

question: Fuel vents are provided in aircraft fuel tanks:
option_a: Have an earth lead between ground, fuel truck, fuel nozzle and the aircraft
option_b: Full tanks will minimize the condensation forming overnight
option_c: To allow atmospheric pressure to be retained in the tank as the fuel is used
option_d: Prevent the fuel from surging about during the flight
correct_answer: To allow atmospheric pressure to be retained in the tank as the fuel is used
explanation: The tank vent admits air as fuel is used, keeping tank pressure close to atmospheric pressure. Without it, a vacuum can form and interrupt fuel flow to the engine.

question: The correct sequence for increasing power in an aeroplane with a Constant Speed Unit (CSU) is:
option_a: Richen the mixture, increase RPM, then increase manifold pressure
option_b: Richen the mixture, decrease RPM, then increase manifold pressure
option_c: leanen the mixture, increase RPM, then increase manifold pressure
option_d: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
correct_answer: Richen the mixture, increase RPM, then increase manifold pressure
explanation: When increasing power, select rich mixture and higher RPM before raising manifold pressure. This avoids imposing high cylinder pressure while the engine is turning too slowly; reduce power in the reverse order.

question: Applying carburettor heat allows:
option_a: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
option_b: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_c: Regulate the flow of fuel from the float chamber to the diffuser
option_d: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be increased
correct_answer: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
explanation: The carburettor-heat system selects air warmed by a shroud around the exhaust. That heat prevents or melts induction ice, although the lower air density normally reduces power.

question: Carburetor icing is most likely to occur:
option_a: At the venturi butterfly valve or inlet manifold
correct_answer: At the venturi butterfly valve or inlet manifold
explanation: Air pressure and temperature fall in the venturi, while fuel vaporization removes additional heat. Ice therefore forms most readily around the throttle butterfly and nearby venturi or inlet surfaces.

question: The function of the butterfly valve in a carburettor is to:
option_a: At the venturi butterfly valve or inlet manifold
option_b: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
option_c: The engine starting to run rough and a decrease in RPM
option_d: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
correct_answer: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
explanation: The butterfly is the throttle valve. Changing its opening controls how much fuel-air mixture can enter the inlet manifold and therefore controls engine power.

question: The fuel supply line from the fuel tank to the engine normally:
option_a: Draws fuel from a position higher than the sump to allow water or other impurities to settle at the bottom of the tank
option_b: To allow atmospheric pressure to be retained in the tank as the fuel is used
option_c: Prevent the fuel from surging about during the flight
option_d: A fuel vent in the fuel tank cap
correct_answer: Draws fuel from a position higher than the sump to allow water or other impurities to settle at the bottom of the tank
explanation: The normal fuel pickup is positioned above the lowest sump so water and sediment can settle below it rather than flow directly to the engine. The sump must still be drained during pre-flight.

question: In a piston engine, the piston will have passed TDC and be moving towards BDC during:
correct_answer: The induction and power strokes
explanation: After top dead centre, the piston travels down on induction as it draws in a fresh charge, and down on the power stroke as expanding combustion gases drive it.

question: When the mixture control lever is moved to the full lean position:
option_a: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be increased
option_b: The mixture should be in the full lean position until the engine fires and then richened slowly to keep the engine running
option_c: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_d: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be decreased
correct_answer: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be decreased
explanation: Full lean restricts fuel flow into the induction system. In many aircraft it also reaches idle cut-off, stopping fuel at the low-power metering circuit; the POH defines the exact operation.

question: When attempting to start an engine which has been over-primed or flooded:
option_a: The mixture should be in the full lean position until the engine fires and then richened slowly to keep the engine running
option_b: Feeds air from within the engine cowling to the induction system
option_c: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
option_d: Provide extra fuel when the throttle is opened rapidly
correct_answer: The mixture should be in the full lean position until the engine fires and then richened slowly to keep the engine running
explanation: A flooded engine already contains excess fuel, so the starting procedure must prevent still more fuel entering until a combustible ratio returns. Use the aircraft's published flooded-start procedure and enrich only after the engine fires.

question: The presence of carburettor icing would be indicated by:
option_a: The engine starting to run rough and a increase in RPM
option_b: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
option_c: The engine starting to run rough and a decrease in RPM
correct_answer: The engine starting to run rough and a decrease in RPM
explanation: Carburettor ice restricts airflow and disturbs mixture distribution. In a fixed-pitch aircraft the usual signs are falling RPM, rough running, and gradual power loss.

question: An accelerator pump is often incorporated in a carburettor in order to:
option_b: Heated air from around the exhaust to enter the carburettor
option_c: The engine starting to run rough and a decrease in RPM
option_d: Provide extra fuel when the throttle is opened rapidly
correct_answer: Provide extra fuel when the throttle is opened rapidly
explanation: Opening the throttle rapidly admits air faster than the normal fuel circuit can respond, causing a temporary lean mixture. The accelerator pump supplies a brief extra shot of fuel to prevent hesitation.

question: To eliminate the risk of fire when refuelling:
option_a: To allow atmospheric pressure to be retained in the tank as the fuel is used
option_b: Full tanks will minimize the condensation forming overnight
option_c: Have an earth lead between ground, fuel truck, fuel nozzle and the aircraft
option_d: Prevent the fuel from surging about during the flight
correct_answer: Have an earth lead between ground, fuel truck, fuel nozzle and the aircraft
explanation: Bonding the aircraft, fuel vehicle, nozzle, and ground equalizes their electrical potential. This prevents a static spark from igniting flammable fuel vapour.

question: In respect of piston engine operation, a rich mixture is one where:
correct_answer: The fuel-to-air ratio is increased
explanation: A rich mixture contains a greater mass of fuel for a given mass of air. It can aid cooling and high-power operation, but excessive richness wastes fuel and can foul plugs.

question: The correct sequence of the four strokes of a piston engine is:
correct_answer: Induction, compression, power, exhaust
explanation: The four strokes occur over two crankshaft revolutions: induction draws in the charge, compression squeezes it, power extracts work from combustion, and exhaust expels the burned gases.

question: With reference to fixed pitch propeller:
option_a: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
option_b: A coarse pitch propeller will produce a better cruise performance than a fine pitch propeller
option_c: Richen the mixture, increase RPM, then increase manifold pressure
option_d: Bending the blade in the opposite direction to the rotation
correct_answer: A coarse pitch propeller will produce a better cruise performance than a fine pitch propeller
explanation: A coarse fixed-pitch propeller is efficient at higher forward speeds because its larger blade angle suits the flatter relative airflow in cruise. A fine pitch is better for take-off and climb.

question: During the operation of a reciprocating engine the piston is travelling down during:
correct_answer: The induction and power strokes
explanation: The piston descends on induction to increase cylinder volume and draw in the charge. It descends again on the power stroke as expanding gases turn the crankshaft.

question: With regard to the engine handling:
option_a: Allow air to mix with the fuel before it is discharged into the venturi as the power is increased
option_b: Feeds air from within the engine cowling to the induction system
option_c: The throttle should be opened and closed smoothly to avoid overstressing the crankshaft
option_d: Control the volume of fuel-air mixture entering the engine
correct_answer: The throttle should be opened and closed smoothly to avoid overstressing the crankshaft
explanation: Rapid throttle movement creates abrupt pressure and torque changes in the cylinders and crankshaft. Smooth movement lets fuel metering and engine loads change progressively.

question: An engine which starts to run rough and then slowly loses power is probably suffering from:
correct_answer: Carburetor icing
explanation: Carburettor ice usually builds gradually, restricting the induction path. The engine first runs rough and then loses power as airflow becomes increasingly limited.

question: A manually operated primer pump should always be used to prime a cold engine for start because:
option_a: The mixture should be in the full lean position until the engine fires and then richened slowly to keep the engine running
option_b: The throttle should be opened and closed smoothly to avoid overstressing the crankshaft
option_c: The primer delivers fuel directly into the induction system near the inlet valves
option_d: Will also richen the mixture because of the higher air temperature
correct_answer: The primer delivers fuel directly into the induction system near the inlet valves
explanation: Cold fuel vaporizes poorly during cranking. The primer places a measured quantity near the inlet valves, where it can form an ignitable mixture without depending on venturi airflow.

question: A fuel pressure gauge is usually incorporated in aircraft fuel systems to measure the pressure of the fuel:
correct_answer: As it enters the carburettor
explanation: Measuring pressure at the carburettor inlet confirms that the pumps and fuel lines are delivering fuel at the pressure required by the metering system.

question: Application of "alternate air" in a fuel injection system:
option_a: The primer delivers fuel directly into the induction system near the inlet valves
option_b: Feeds air from within the engine cowling to the induction system
option_c: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be decreased
option_d: The amount of fuel entering the inlet manifold will be increased
correct_answer: Feeds air from within the engine cowling to the induction system
explanation: Alternate air bypasses a blocked or iced normal intake and draws air from inside the cowling. This air is usually warmer and may be unfiltered, but it restores engine airflow.

question: 100 LL aviation fuel or AVGAS can be identified by its:
correct_answer: Blue colour
explanation: 100LL avgas is dyed blue so its grade can be identified visually. Colour is a cross-check only; the required fuel grade must still be confirmed from the aircraft documentation and fuel markings.

question: Atmospheric pressure is maintained within the fuel tanks through the use of:
option_b: A fuel vent in the fuel tank cap
correct_answer: A fuel vent in the fuel tank cap
explanation: A vent in the cap or tank replaces the volume of fuel consumed with air. This prevents a fuel-flow-restricting vacuum and allows the tank to remain near atmospheric pressure.

question: The function of a diffuser in a carburettor is to:
option_b: Allow air to mix with the fuel before it is discharged into the venturi as the power is increased
correct_answer: Allow air to mix with the fuel before it is discharged into the venturi as the power is increased
explanation: The diffuser introduces air into the metered fuel before discharge, producing a fine fuel-air emulsion. Better atomization helps the fuel mix uniformly with the main venturi airflow.

question: The absorption of water into aviation fuel is:
option_a: Unaffected by the temperature of the fuel
option_d: Impossible, because water does not mix with fuel
correct_answer: More likely with warm fuel
explanation: Warm fuel can hold more dissolved water than cold fuel, so absorption is more likely when the fuel is warm. As the fuel cools, overnight or at altitude, the dissolved water comes out of suspension as free droplets that settle in the sump or can freeze, which is why the tanks must be drained before flight.

question: On an aeroplane equipped with a constant-speed unit, RPM has been selected. If power is then slowly increased, RPM will:
correct_answer: Remain the same
explanation: A constant-speed unit senses an RPM change and varies blade angle to oppose it. When engine power increases, the governor coarsens the blades so the selected RPM remains constant.

question: When leaning the air/fuel mixture:
option_a: The ratio of air to fuel decreases
option_c: The ratio of air to fuel increases
correct_answer: The ratio of air to fuel increases
explanation: Leaning reduces fuel flow while airflow changes little, so the air-to-fuel ratio increases. Correct leaning restores efficiency as air density falls with altitude.

question: One of the advantages of refuelling an aeroplane with full fuel after flight is that:
option_a: Full tanks will minimize the condensation forming overnight
option_b: Prevent the fuel from surging about during the flight
option_d: Have an earth lead between ground, fuel truck, fuel nozzle and the aircraft
correct_answer: Full tanks will minimize the condensation forming overnight
explanation: A full tank contains less moist air space above the fuel. With less air available to cool and condense overnight, less water is likely to collect in the tank.

question: When the throttle is opened from idle to full power rapidly, additional fuel is required to compensate for the increased volume of air. This is provided by:
correct_answer: The accelerator pump
explanation: A rapid throttle opening produces an immediate airflow increase but the normal fuel circuit responds more slowly. The accelerator pump bridges that delay with additional fuel.

question: The mixing of fuel and air in a carburettor is achieved:
correct_answer: By the diffuser
explanation: The diffuser, or discharge nozzle system, introduces metered fuel into the high-speed venturi airflow and helps atomize it. This is where the main fuel-air mixing process begins.

question: The helix angle of a propeller is the angle:
option_a: Ensure that the thrust produced is constant along the propeller blade
option_c: A coarse pitch propeller will produce a better cruise performance than a fine pitch propeller
option_d: Between the relative airflow and the plane of rotation
correct_answer: Between the relative airflow and the plane of rotation
explanation: Helix angle is measured between the local relative airflow approaching a blade section and the propeller's plane of rotation. It changes with both rotational speed and forward speed.

question: If A/C, with a fixed pitch propeller is placed in a shallow dive so that forward speed increases with no change in power setting, RPM will:
correct_answer: Increase
explanation: In a dive, increased forward airflow reduces the fixed-pitch blade's effective loading and tends to drive the propeller faster. With no governor to change pitch, engine RPM rises.

question: The pilot of an aircraft which is equipped with manifold pressure gauge would be able to identify the presence of carburettor icing by:
correct_answer: A decrease in manifold pressure
explanation: Ice narrows the carburettor throat and reduces the pressure delivered to the inlet manifold. On an aircraft with a constant-speed propeller, falling manifold pressure is often the first clear indication.

question: When the throttle is opened quickly, the accelerator pump will:
option_a: Discharge additional fuel into the venturi
correct_answer: Discharge additional fuel into the venturi
explanation: The accelerator pump is linked to rapid throttle movement and discharges an extra quantity of fuel into the venturi. This prevents a momentary lean cut as airflow increases.

question: The type of fuel supply system in which the fuel tank is constructed as an integral part of the wing structure is called:
correct_answer: A wet wing
explanation: A wet wing uses sealed sections of the wing structure itself as the fuel tank. It eliminates a separate tank but relies on sound structural joints and sealant to prevent leaks.

question: High oil temperature together with low oil pressure indicates:
option_c: Are an indication of low oil supply
correct_answer: Are an indication of low oil supply
explanation: A low oil quantity leaves less oil to absorb and reject heat, so temperature rises. Once the pump begins drawing air or cannot maintain flow, oil pressure falls; together these indications warn of a serious lubrication problem.

question: The most appropriate method to deal with pre-ignition in a piston engine during flight is:
option_a: decrease engine cooling and enrich the mixture
option_b: Increase engine cooling and enrich the mixture
option_c: Increase engine cooling and enlean the mixture
option_d: The inlet valve opening prior to the piston reaching TDC
correct_answer: Increase engine cooling and enrich the mixture
explanation: Pre-ignition is caused by a hot spot igniting the charge before the normal spark. Reducing temperature is urgent: enrich the mixture and increase cooling in accordance with the POH, while reducing power if required.

question: The lubricating system of a piston engine normally makes use of:
option_a: Before the oil enters the engine components
option_b: Before being fed to the engine components
option_c: A gear type pump combined with splash lubrication
option_d: Maintain a constant oil pressure over a range of engine power changes
correct_answer: A gear type pump combined with splash lubrication
explanation: A positive-displacement gear pump supplies pressurized oil to bearings and other critical parts. Oil thrown from moving components also provides splash lubrication to cylinder walls and related surfaces.

question: The breather pipe on an engine is used to:
correct_answer: Relieve excess sump pressure
explanation: The breather keeps crankcase or sump pressure close to atmospheric pressure. Without it, blow-by gases could pressurize the sump, force oil past seals, and interfere with oil return.

question: The crankshaft of a piston engine is balanced by the addition of counter- weights in order to:
option_a: Counter-weights attached to the crank cheeks
option_b: Reduce vibration caused by power impulses on the opposite crankpin
option_c: Control the flow of air over the engine cylinders in order to maintain the correct operating temperature
option_d: Direct the airflow over the engine cylinders for better cooling
correct_answer: Reduce vibration caused by power impulses on the opposite crankpin
explanation: Counterweights oppose the unbalanced forces and moments created by reciprocating parts and uneven power impulses. Reducing vibration protects crankshaft bearings and other engine components.

question: The colour of Phosphate Ester hydraulic fluid is:
correct_answer: Purple
explanation: Phosphate-ester hydraulic fluid is identified by a purple colour. Hydraulic-fluid families are chemically different, so colour and the aircraft manual must be checked before servicing.

question: Unless approved for use, the use of motor car fuel (MOGAS) in aircraft engines:
option_a: When fuel of too low an octane rating is used
option_b: Should not be used because it may result in detonation, reduced power and lead fouling of the spark plugs
option_c: The short period that both inlet and exhaust valves are both open around TDC
option_d: The inlet valve closes after the piston has passed bottom dead centre
correct_answer: Should not be used because it may result in detonation, reduced power and lead fouling of the spark plugs
explanation: Automotive fuel must be used only when the aircraft and engine are specifically approved for it. Unsuitable volatility and combustion characteristics can cause vapour lock, detonation, deposits, and reduced power.

question: Engine cylinders and barrels are usually fitted with the fins in order to:
correct_answer: Improve engine cooling
explanation: Cooling fins increase the cylinder's surface area exposed to airflow. More surface area allows combustion heat to pass into the air more quickly.

question: Blue smoke appearing from the exhaust pipes of a piston engine which is running is an indication that the engine:
correct_answer: Is burning oil
explanation: Blue exhaust smoke is characteristic of lubricating oil burning in the cylinders. Possible sources include worn rings, valve guides, or excessive oil entering the combustion chamber.

question: Detonation may occur in a piston engine:
option_d: When fuel of too low an octane rating is used
correct_answer: When fuel of too low an octane rating is used
explanation: Octane rating measures resistance to detonation. Fuel below the specified grade can auto-ignite the remaining charge after the spark, creating damaging pressure waves.

question: Normal operation of a piston engine would be indicated on the firing end of a spark plug by:
correct_answer: A light grey coating
explanation: A light grey or light tan deposit normally indicates that combustion temperature and mixture strength are within a healthy range. Wet oil or heavy black soot points to a fault.

question: An oil pressure gauge is usually located in the oil line of a wet sump system:
option_a: after the oil enters the engine components
option_b: Before the oil enters the engine components
correct_answer: Before the oil enters the engine components
explanation: The pressure gauge connection is placed downstream of the pump but before oil reaches the main galleries and components. It therefore shows the pressure actually available to lubricate the engine.

question: Dry sump piston engine lubrication systems make use of a scavenge pump to:
option_d: Pump oil from the sump back to the oil tank
correct_answer: Pump oil from the sump back to the oil tank
explanation: A dry-sump engine stores oil in a separate tank. The scavenge pump removes oil from the crankcase and returns it to that tank, preventing oil from accumulating in the sump.

question: The oil in a wet sump lubrication system passes through the oil cooler:
option_a: after being fed to the engine components
option_c: Before being fed to the engine components
correct_answer: Before being fed to the engine components
explanation: Cooling the oil before it enters the engine lowers the temperature of the lubricant supplied to bearings and pistons. The oil can then absorb more engine heat while maintaining suitable viscosity.

question: The component of hydraulic system which stores the hydraulic fluid under pressure is called:
correct_answer: The accumulator
explanation: An accumulator stores energy by using hydraulic pressure to compress a gas charge. It can smooth pressure fluctuations and supply short bursts of fluid when demand exceeds pump output.

question: The primary method of cooling oil in a wet sump system is by:
option_d: Ram air through an oil cooler
correct_answer: Ram air through an oil cooler
explanation: Ram air passing through the oil cooler removes heat from the circulating oil. The cooler acts as a small heat exchanger between the oil and the outside airflow.

question: The temperature of the oil in a wet sump lubrication system is usually measured:
correct_answer: After leaving the oil cooler
explanation: Measuring temperature after the cooler indicates the condition of the oil being delivered to the engine. This is the oil whose viscosity must remain suitable for effective lubrication.

question: Ignition of fuel/air mixture in a four-stroke piston engine occurs during the:
correct_answer: Compression stroke
explanation: The spark occurs late in the compression stroke, normally before TDC. This gives the flame time to develop so peak cylinder pressure occurs just after TDC on the power stroke.

question: The most appropriate method to deal with detonation during flight is to:
option_a: Reduce power and enlean the mixture
option_c: Reduce power and enrich the mixture
correct_answer: Reduce power and enrich the mixture
explanation: Detonation is promoted by high pressure and temperature. Reducing power lowers cylinder pressure, while enriching the mixture increases charge cooling; follow the POH and land if abnormal operation continues.

question: The colour of Vegetable Based hydraulic fluid is:
correct_answer: Blue
explanation: Vegetable-based hydraulic fluid is traditionally identified by a blue colour. The colour code helps prevent use of an incompatible fluid, but the maintenance specification remains controlling.

question: The colour of Mineral Based hydraulic fluid is:
correct_answer: Red
explanation: Mineral-based hydraulic fluid is normally dyed red for identification. It must not be confused or mixed with chemically incompatible vegetable or phosphate-ester fluids.

question: Valve overlap in the four-stroke piston engine will occur between the:
correct_answer: Exhaust and the induction strokes
explanation: Valve overlap occurs at the transition from exhaust to induction near TDC. The exhaust valve has not fully closed when the inlet valve begins opening, improving gas flow at operating speed.

question: An accumulator may be installed in a hydraulic system in order to:
option_a: Store hydraulic fluid under pressure for peak demand or emergency use
option_b: Allow the fluid level to expand and contract as fluid is used in the system
option_d: Prevent a vacuum from forming by allowing air into the reservoir as the fluid is drawn off
correct_answer: Store hydraulic fluid under pressure for peak demand or emergency use
explanation: An accumulator stores pressurized fluid by compressing a gas charge. The stored energy can meet peak demand, damp pump pulsations, or operate a service briefly after pump failure.

question: A non-pressurized hydraulic fluid reservoir is fitted with an air vent, often in the cap, in order to:
option_a: Allow the fluid level to contract and contract as fluid is used in the system
option_b: Allow the fluid level to expand and contract as fluid is used in the system
option_c: Allow the fluid level to expand and expand as fluid is used in the system
option_d: Store hydraulic fluid under pressure for peak demand or emergency use
correct_answer: Allow the fluid level to expand and contract as fluid is used in the system
explanation: As a non-pressurized reservoir supplies or receives fluid, its liquid level changes. The vent allows air to enter or leave so a vacuum or unwanted pressure cannot oppose fluid flow.

question: The type of pump utilised in a piston engine to provide high pressure oil lubrication is a:
correct_answer: Gear type pump
explanation: A gear pump is a positive-displacement pump: meshing gears carry a fixed volume of oil from inlet to outlet. It can maintain the pressure and flow needed by engine bearings.

question: In a wet sump piston engine lubrication system:
option_a: Oil is supplied only by splash lubrication
option_b: Oil is stored only in an external tank
option_c: Oil is mixed directly with the fuel
option_d: Oil is stored in the engine sump and distributed throughout the engine by a pressure pump
correct_answer: Oil is stored in the engine sump and distributed throughout the engine by a pressure pump
explanation: In a wet-sump system, the crankcase sump is both the collection point and the oil reservoir. A pressure pump draws from it and distributes oil through the engine galleries.

question: Balancing of the crankshaft of a piston engine is achieved by:
option_d: Counter-weights attached to the crank cheeks
correct_answer: Counter-weights attached to the crank cheeks
explanation: Counterweights attached to the crank cheeks oppose the inertia and combustion loads acting on the crankshaft. Correct balance reduces vibration and bearing stress.

question: Vegetable and mineral hydraulic fluids can be mixed in the same hydraulic system:
correct_answer: Never
explanation: Vegetable- and mineral-based hydraulic fluids must not be mixed. Incompatible fluids can attack seals, change viscosity, form deposits, and lead to system failure.

question: A condition that may occur in only one cylinder as a result of an excessively lean mixture is:
correct_answer: Pre-ignition
explanation: An excessively lean mixture can make one cylinder run especially hot. A glowing deposit, valve, or spark-plug electrode may then ignite the charge early, causing pre-ignition.

question: After starting an engine black smoke is seen coming from the exhaust. This indicates:
option_a: That the mixture is too lean
option_c: That the mixture is too rich
correct_answer: That the mixture is too rich
explanation: Black exhaust smoke indicates excess fuel and incomplete combustion. The mixture is too rich for the available air, often after over-priming or an incorrect mixture setting.

question: Counter-weights are attached to the crankshaft of an engine in order to:
correct_answer: Prevent damage from vibrations
explanation: Crankshaft counterweights reduce unbalanced forces and torsional vibration. Without adequate balance, repeated vibration can fatigue bearings, mounts, and the crankshaft itself.

question: Lubrication of the main bearings and crankshaft of the engine is provided:
option_a: A gear type pump combined with splash lubrication
option_b: By both high-pressure oil and splash lubrication
option_c: Before the oil enters the engine components
option_d: Before being fed to the engine components
correct_answer: By both high-pressure oil and splash lubrication
explanation: Pressurized oil is routed to heavily loaded bearings and crankshaft passages, where a reliable oil film is essential. Oil flung from rotating parts provides additional splash lubrication.

question: Using fuel of a higher octane than recommended may result in:
option_a: Immediate failure of the fuel pump
option_b: A permanent increase in engine power
option_c: Lead fouling of the spark plugs
correct_answer: Lead fouling of the spark plugs
explanation: Some higher-octane avgas grades contain more lead than the grade specified for a low-compression engine. At unsuitable temperatures, lead deposits can foul spark plugs; always use an approved grade.

question: Loss of pressure in a hydraulic system is indicated to the pilot:
correct_answer: A warning light usually red
explanation: A pressure switch monitors hydraulic-system pressure and illuminates a red warning light when it falls below the safe threshold. The warning indicates loss of pressure, not necessarily the exact failed component.

question: The purpose of the pressure relief valve in a lubrication system is to:
option_a: Maintain a constant oil pressure over a range of engine power changes
option_b: By both high-pressure oil and splash lubrication
option_c: Oil is stored in the engine sump and distributed throughout the engine by a pressure pump
option_d: A gear type pump combined with splash lubrication
correct_answer: Maintain a constant oil pressure over a range of engine power changes
explanation: The relief valve opens a bypass path when oil pressure exceeds its setting. Diverting excess pump flow prevents damaging pressure while keeping system pressure reasonably constant as RPM changes.

question: The primary purpose of a cowl-flap is to:
option_a: Reduce vibration caused by power impulses on the opposite crankpin
option_b: Direct the airflow over the engine cylinders for better cooling
option_c: Control the flow of air over the engine cylinders in order to maintain the correct operating temperature
option_d: Counter-weights attached to the crank cheeks
correct_answer: Control the flow of air over the engine cylinders in order to maintain the correct operating temperature
explanation: Opening cowl flaps increases cooling airflow through the engine compartment; closing them reduces cooling drag. The pilot uses them to keep cylinder and oil temperatures within limits.

question: If the RPM of an aircraft's piston engine is increased, the ignition timing will:
correct_answer: Remain the same
explanation: Once the starting retard or impulse coupling disengages, a conventional magneto fires at a fixed crankshaft angle. Increasing RPM changes how often sparks occur, not the specified ignition angle.

question: The purpose of the vent on a hydraulic fluid reservoir is to:
option_a: Prevent a vacuum from forming by allowing air into the reservoir as the fluid is drawn off
option_b: Store hydraulic fluid under pressure for peak demand or emergency use
option_c: Allow the fluid level to expand and contract as fluid is used in the system
option_d: When pressure is increased on a confined volume of fluid the increased pressure will be transmitted by the fluid
correct_answer: Prevent a vacuum from forming by allowing air into the reservoir as the fluid is drawn off
explanation: The reservoir vent admits air as fluid is drawn into the system and releases air as fluid returns. This keeps the reservoir near atmospheric pressure and prevents a flow-restricting vacuum.

question: The timing of the ignition of the fuel and air mixture in an internal combustion engine is arranged to occur:
option_a: Between 20 degrees and 25 degrees after TDC during the compression stroke
option_b: Increase engine cooling and enrich the mixture
option_c: Between 20 degrees and 25 degrees before TDC during the compression stroke
option_d: When fuel of too low an octane rating is used
correct_answer: Between 20 degrees and 25 degrees before TDC during the compression stroke
explanation: Ignition is advanced before TDC because combustion takes time. A spark roughly 20 to 25 degrees before TDC lets maximum useful pressure develop just after the piston begins the power stroke.

question: Dry, black, powdery carbon on the firing end of a spark plug usually indicates:
correct_answer: An excessively rich mixture
explanation: Dry, black, powdery soot is carbon produced by incomplete combustion, most commonly from an over-rich mixture. Oily, wet deposits would instead suggest oil entering the combustion chamber.

question: The supply of electrical power to the engine starter motor is controlled by:
option_c: A solenoid located near the starter motor
correct_answer: A solenoid located near the starter motor
explanation: The starter motor draws far more current than the cockpit switch can safely carry. A nearby solenoid uses a small control current to close heavy contacts in the short, high-current starter circuit.

question: A hydraulic system operates on the basic principle that:
option_a: Fluid pressure decreases equally in all directions
option_b: Pressure acts only in the direction of flow
option_c: A confined fluid can be compressed easily
option_d: When pressure is increased on a confined volume of fluid the increased pressure will be transmitted by the fluid
correct_answer: When pressure is increased on a confined volume of fluid the increased pressure will be transmitted by the fluid
explanation: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to a confined incompressible fluid is transmitted equally throughout the fluid. Different piston areas can therefore multiply force.

question: The term "valve overlap" refers to:
option_a: The short period that both inlet and exhaust valves are both open around TDC
option_b: The inlet valve closes after the piston has passed bottom dead centre
option_c: The inlet valve opening prior to the piston reaching TDC
option_d: Where there are hot spots in one or more cylinders
correct_answer: The short period that both inlet and exhaust valves are both open around TDC
explanation: Valve overlap is the brief period around TDC when the exhaust valve is still open and the inlet valve has already opened. Gas momentum improves cylinder scavenging and filling.

question: The cylinder head temperature gauge usually obtains its reading from:
option_a: A cylinder which tests show runs the hottest
correct_answer: A cylinder which tests show runs the hottest
explanation: The temperature probe is installed on the cylinder known by testing to run hottest. Keeping that cylinder within its limit provides protection for the cooler cylinders as well.

question: Pre-ignition is likely to occur in a piston engine:
option_a: Increase engine cooling and enrich the mixture
option_b: The inlet valve opening prior to the piston reaching TDC
option_c: The inlet valve closes after the piston has passed bottom dead centre
option_d: Where there are hot spots in one or more cylinders
correct_answer: Where there are hot spots in one or more cylinders
explanation: A hot spot such as a glowing carbon deposit, overheated valve, or spark-plug electrode can ignite the mixture before the timed spark. This early combustion is pre-ignition.

question: The use of fuel with a lower octane rating than that recommended by the aircraft manufacturer may lead to:
correct_answer: Detonation
explanation: Using fuel with insufficient octane reduces the margin against spontaneous end-gas ignition. The resulting detonation produces sharp pressure waves, overheating, and possible engine damage.

question: The purpose of baffles in the engine compartments is to:
option_a: Control the flow of air over the engine cylinders in order to maintain the correct operating temperature
option_b: Direct the airflow over the engine cylinders for better cooling
option_d: Reduce vibration caused by power impulses on the opposite crankpin
correct_answer: Direct the airflow over the engine cylinders for better cooling
explanation: Baffles prevent cooling air from taking an easy path around the engine. They force it closely over and between cylinder fins so each cylinder receives effective cooling.

question: A low-pressure filter is usually incorporated in a hydraulic system between:
correct_answer: The reservoir and the pump
explanation: A low-pressure filter is fitted in the suction line between the reservoir and pump to remove contamination before it reaches the pump. It must provide adequate flow to avoid pump cavitation.

question: In a simple airspeed indicator, pitot pressure is supplied to:
option_a: Pitot pressure is fed to the capsule
correct_answer: Pitot pressure is fed to the capsule
explanation: Pitot, or total, pressure is applied inside the flexible capsule. Static pressure surrounds it in the case, so the capsule responds to the difference between total and static pressure.

question: A centre zero ammeter is incorporated in an electrical system to:
option_b: Are that positive indications are shown right of centre
option_c: As a means of preventing the system from becoming overloaded
option_d: Indicate the flow of current into and out of battery
correct_answer: Indicate the flow of current into and out of battery
explanation: A centre-zero ammeter is placed in the battery lead. A deflection to the charge side shows current entering the battery; a deflection to the discharge side shows the battery supplying the system.

question: A reverse current cut-out relay, or circuit breaker, is used in a generator supplied electrical system to:
option_a: Indicate alternator or generator output current only
option_b: Prevent the flow of current from the battery to the generator
correct_answer: Prevent the flow of current from the battery to the generator
explanation: When generator voltage falls below battery voltage, the cut-out opens the circuit. This prevents the battery driving current backward through the generator and turning it into a motor.

question: In order to generate electrical power, an aircraft magneto depends on:
correct_answer: Rotating magnet
explanation: An engine-driven magnet rotates relative to coils inside the magneto. The changing magnetic flux induces electrical energy, so normal ignition does not depend on the aircraft battery.

question: The electrical current produced by a magneto:
option_a: Is produced by the starter motor
option_b: Is induced by the alternator stator
option_c: Is supplied by the aircraft battery
option_d: Is created by the rotating magnet
correct_answer: Is created by the rotating magnet
explanation: The rotating magnet creates a changing magnetic field through the magneto coils. Electromagnetic induction first produces current in the primary circuit and then a high voltage for the spark plugs.

question: In the event that a fuse in an electrical circuit has blown:
option_a: Are that positive indications are shown right of centre
option_b: It should be replaced only once with a fuse of same value
correct_answer: It should be replaced only once with a fuse of same value
explanation: A replacement fuse must have the specified current rating; a higher rating can let wiring overheat. If the replacement also blows, leave the circuit isolated because a fault is still present.

question: Control of the voltage output from a DC generator is achieved through a:
correct_answer: Voltage regulator
explanation: The voltage regulator varies generator field current so output voltage remains within the required range as engine speed and electrical load change.

question: Diodes are used in an AC alternator to:
option_b: Convert the AC output to DC
correct_answer: Convert the AC output to DC
explanation: Alternator windings generate alternating current. Diodes conduct in only one direction, forming a rectifier that supplies the direct current required by the aircraft system and battery.

question: Modern aircraft electrical systems generally make use of circuit breakers:
option_c: Prevent the flow of current from the battery to the generator
option_d: As a means of preventing the system from becoming overloaded
correct_answer: As a means of preventing the system from becoming overloaded
explanation: A circuit breaker opens when current exceeds a safe value, protecting wiring from overheating and fire. It protects the circuit conductors rather than the connected appliance alone.

question: The function of the distributor in a magneto is to:
option_a: The engine will continue to run with the magneto switch in the off position
option_b: Produce a low voltage to the transformer when you turn magneto's switch on start position
option_c: The power output of an alternator will be greater at a lower RPM
option_d: Route high voltage to each spark plug in the correct firing order
correct_answer: Route high voltage to each spark plug in the correct firing order
explanation: The distributor rotor connects the magneto's high-voltage output to each plug lead in sequence. Correct synchronization ensures each cylinder receives its spark at the required time.

question: A breakage or disconnection of the magneto earth wire will have the effect of:
option_a: The engine will continue to run with the magneto switch in the off position
option_b: The power output of an alternator will be greater at a lower RPM
option_c: Making it impossible to stop the engine by switching off the ignition
option_d: Produce a low voltage to the transformer when you turn magneto's switch on start position
correct_answer: Making it impossible to stop the engine by switching off the ignition
explanation: The magneto is switched off by grounding its primary circuit through the earth, or P-lead. If that wire breaks, the magneto remains live and the engine may continue running with the switch OFF.

question: A left-zero ammeter is incorporated in an electrical system to:
option_b: As a means of preventing the system from becoming overloaded
option_c: Indicate alternator or generator output current only
correct_answer: Indicate alternator or generator output current only
explanation: A left-zero ammeter, often used as a loadmeter, shows the current being produced by the alternator or generator. It does not directly distinguish battery charge from discharge.

question: In a DC generator, The AC output is converted into DC through:
correct_answer: A commutator
explanation: The voltage generated in a rotating DC-generator armature is alternating internally. The segmented commutator reverses the coil connections each half-turn, producing a unidirectional output at the brushes.

question: The indications of a centre-zero ammeter:
option_a: Are that positive indications are shown right of centre
option_b: Are that positive indications are shown left of centre
option_c: It should be replaced only once with a fuse of same value
option_d: Indicate alternator or generator output current only
correct_answer: Are that positive indications are shown right of centre
explanation: On a centre-zero ammeter, a right-of-centre positive indication normally means current is flowing into the battery. A left or negative indication means the battery is discharging.

question: An operational advantage of the alternator is that it:
option_a: The power output of an alternator will be greater at a lower RPM
option_b: Control the voltage output from a DC generator
option_c: Will still produce electrical power at low RPM
option_d: Convert direct current to alternating current
correct_answer: Will still produce electrical power at low RPM
explanation: An alternator can produce useful output at relatively low engine speed because of its rotating field and efficient stationary windings. This is valuable during taxi and other low-RPM operation.

question: The storage capacity of a battery is usually expressed in:
correct_answer: Ampere-hours
explanation: Ampere-hours describe how much charge a battery can theoretically deliver: current multiplied by time. Actual endurance is lower and varies with discharge rate, temperature, and battery condition.

question: The purpose of an ammeter is to:
correct_answer: Measure electrical current flow
explanation: An ammeter indicates current flow in amperes. Depending on its location, it may show battery charge/discharge or total generator/alternator output.

question: If the earth wire from a magneto to the aircraft structure is broken:
option_a: Supply the aircraft electrical system and recharge the battery
option_b: The engine will continue to run with the magneto switch in the off position
option_c: Produce a low voltage to the transformer when you turn magneto's switch on start position
option_d: Control the voltage output from a DC generator
correct_answer: The engine will continue to run with the magneto switch in the off position
explanation: Opening the ignition switch normally grounds the magneto through its P-lead. A broken earth wire prevents grounding, leaving a 'hot' magneto that can produce a spark whenever the engine turns.

question: Pitot pressure is taken from:
option_b: A tube mounted in the relative airflow
correct_answer: A tube mounted in the relative airflow
explanation: A forward-facing pitot tube brings the relative airflow to rest at its opening and senses total pressure. It must be aligned with clean airflow and kept free of water, ice, and insects.

question: In an alternator, the stator:
correct_answer: Remains stationary
explanation: The stator is the stationary set of windings surrounding the alternator rotor. The rotating magnetic field induces AC in these windings without passing the heavy output through brushes.

question: The correct level of electrolyte in a lead acid battery should be maintained by the addition of:
correct_answer: Distilled water
explanation: Normal charging consumes water but leaves the sulphuric acid behind, so only distilled water is used to restore level. Adding acid would make the electrolyte too concentrated.

question: Electrical fuses are rated in:
correct_answer: Amperes
explanation: A fuse's ampere rating is the current it can carry safely before its element melts. The replacement must match the approved rating for the protected wiring.

question: The alternate static source draws air from:
correct_answer: Within the cockpit
explanation: The alternate source usually samples pressure inside the cockpit so the instruments still receive static pressure if the external port is blocked. Cockpit pressure is often slightly lower than outside pressure.

question: In comparison to the generator:
option_a: The power output of an alternator will be greater at a higher RPM
option_b: Control the voltage output from a DC generator
option_c: Produce a strong, retarded spark at the low RPM of engine start
option_d: The power output of an alternator will be greater at a lower RPM
correct_answer: The power output of an alternator will be greater at a lower RPM
explanation: Alternators deliver useful current at lower shaft speeds than comparable generators. They are also generally lighter and better able to support the aircraft load during low-RPM operation.

question: A capacitor is incorporated in an electrical circuit to:
correct_answer: Store an electrical charge
explanation: A capacitor stores separated electrical charge on two plates divided by an insulator. It can release that energy later to smooth voltage, suppress interference, or assist another circuit function.
